docs.text:
Sheet Metal Fundamentals (Sac Levha Temelleri) › Overview

# Sheet Metal Fundamentals (Sac Levha Temelleri)

**How to read this file.** Values marked *typical* are engineering-practice ranges that differ between shops, machines and tooling. They are starting points for a design review, never production limits. The authoritative value is the one in the fabricator's capability sheet.

docs.title: Sheet Metal Fundamentals (Sac Levha Temelleri)
docs.text:
Sheet Metal Fundamentals (Sac Levha Temelleri) › 1. What "sheet metal" is

Sheet metal (sac, sac levha) is flat rolled metal, normally 0.4–6 mm thick; above ~6 mm it is usually called plate (levha / kalın sac). Parts are cut flat, formed by bending, joined and finished. Almost every sheet-metal decision follows from one fact: **the part is designed 3D but manufactured from a flat blank**.

docs.title: Sheet Metal Fundamentals (Sac Levha Temelleri)
docs.text:
Sheet Metal Fundamentals (Sac Levha Temelleri) › 2. Manufacturing chain (üretim zinciri)

```text
Material → Cutting (laser / punch / plasma / waterjet) → Deburring →
Forming (press brake bending, rolling, forming tools) → Joining (welding, PEM/clinch,
rivet, screw) → Surface finish (powder coat, galvanizing, passivation, anodizing) →
Assembly → Inspection → Packing
```
A design decision always has a cost and a risk in at least one later step. Ask "what does this do to the next step?"

docs.title: Sheet Metal Fundamentals (Sac Levha Temelleri)
docs.section: 3. Common materials in Türkiye (grade names on quotes and drawings)
docs.text:
Sheet Metal Fundamentals (Sac Levha Temelleri) › 3. Common materials in Türkiye (grade names on quotes and drawings)

| Common TR name | Typical EN designation | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| DKP (soğuk haddelenmiş sac) | DC01 (EN 10130) | Clean surface, good bending, needs paint/coating against rust |
| HRP / siyah sac (sıcak haddelenmiş) | S235JR (EN 10025) or DD11 | Cheaper, scale on surface, thicker gauges |
| Galvaniz sac | DX51D+Z (EN 10346) | Zinc coating is damaged by welding and laser edges; coating mass (e.g. Z100, Z275) must be specified |
| Paslanmaz 304 | 1.4301 / AISI 304 | Austenitic, work-hardens, springback higher than mild steel |
| Paslanmaz 316L | 1.4404 / AISI 316L | Better chloride resistance (marine, chemical) |
| Alüminyum 5754 | EN AW-5754 (AlMg3) | Good formability and weldability, common for enclosures |
| Alüminyum 5052 | EN AW-5052 (AlMg2.5) | Common outside Europe; do not treat as identical to 5754 without checking |
| Alüminyum 1050 | EN AW-1050 | Very soft, low strength |

Equivalence tables are approximate. For anything certified (pressure, food, marine, rail) use the exact standard and the mill certificate (3.1 test certificate / 3.1 sertifika).

Typical stock thicknesses (mm): 0.5 · 0.6 · 0.8 · 1.0 · 1.2 · 1.5 · 2.0 · 2.5 · 3.0 · 4.0 · 5.0 · 6.0 · 8.0 · 10.0. Always confirm that the thickness is stocked in the chosen grade; a 1.25 mm sheet is not a standard grade-independent choice. Thickness tolerance (EN 10131 for cold-rolled, EN 10051 for hot-rolled, EN 485-4 for aluminium) is part of the real part-to-part variation and affects bends and fits.

docs.title: Sheet Metal Fundamentals (Sac Levha Temelleri)
docs.text:
Sheet Metal Fundamentals (Sac Levha Temelleri) › 4. Cutting processes

| Process | Strength | Typical limitation |
|---|---|---|
| Fiber laser | Fast on thin to medium sheet, narrow kerf, fine detail | Heat-affected edge; reflective metals need suitable machine; thick-plate speed drops |
| CO₂ laser | Good edge on thicker mild steel | Slower on thin sheet than fiber |
| Turret punch | Fast for many holes and forms (louvers, ribs), tools create features | Tool library limits shape; burr direction |
| Plasma | Thick plate, low cost | Wider kerf, rougher edge |
| Waterjet | No heat-affected zone, any material | Slow, taper on thick material |

Laser kerf is typically 0.1–0.3 mm depending on thickness, nozzle and material. Nested parts are separated by a web (typically ≥ 1 × thickness, shop dependent).

docs.title: Sheet Metal Fundamentals (Sac Levha Temelleri)
docs.text:
Sheet Metal Fundamentals (Sac Levha Temelleri) › 5. Design rules of thumb (typical values)

All distances in terms of material thickness **T** and inside bend radius **R**. Check against the fabricator.

| Rule | Typical starting value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Inside bend radius | ≥ 1 × T for mild steel; larger for 5xxx/6xxx aluminium, hard tempers, stainless | Cracking on the outside of the bend |
| Minimum flange length (after bend) | ≈ 3–4 × T + R, tooling dependent | Flange must sit on the die shoulder |
| Hole centre-to-bend line | ≥ 2.5 × T + R (hole edge to bend start ≥ ~2 T) | Hole distorts into an oval if too close |
| Slot or cut-out edge to bend | ≥ 3 × T + R | Same distortion |
| Hole diameter (laser, steel) | ≥ ~1 × T | Heat and dross; stainless may need more |
| Hole diameter (punch) | ≥ ~1–1.5 × T | Punch strength |
| Hole edge to sheet edge | ≥ 1.5–2 × T | Tear-out and edge bulge |
| Bend relief width | ≥ T (often ≥ 1.0–1.5 × T) | Prevents bulging and tearing at the end of a bend |
| Bend relief depth | ≥ R + T (+ small margin) | Relief must go past the bend tangent line |
| Hem (closed) | Min. inner radius & flat-length rules are shop specific | Cracks if the material is not annealed enough |
| Grain direction | Bend across the rolling direction when possible, esp. for stainless/aluminium | Cracking along the grain |

docs.title: Sheet Metal Fundamentals (Sac Levha Temelleri)
docs.text:
Sheet Metal Fundamentals (Sac Levha Temelleri) › 6. Features commonly formed in sheet

Louvers (panjur), lances, extruded/tapped holes, embossed ribs (nervür), countersinks, offsets/jogs, hems, flanged holes, dimples. Formed features need a **tool** (standard or custom); a feature that is not in the shop's tool library becomes a custom tool or a different process, with cost and lead time.

docs.title: Sheet Metal Fundamentals (Sac Levha Temelleri)
docs.text:
Sheet Metal Fundamentals (Sac Levha Temelleri) › 7. Tolerances that are realistic

Typical achievable values (shop dependent): laser cut contour ±0.1–0.2 mm; punched features ±0.1–0.2 mm; bend angle ±0.5°–1° (air bending); bend position/leg length ±0.2–0.5 mm accumulating per bend; flatness of larger sheets is limited by the material. A "±0.05" requirement on a bent dimension is normally not realistic and needs measurement and process planning. See `knowledge/07-gdt-and-tolerancing.md` for ISO 2768.

docs.title: Sheet Metal Fundamentals (Sac Levha Temelleri)
docs.text:
Sheet Metal Fundamentals (Sac Levha Temelleri) › 8. Joining (short)

Welding (TIG, MIG/MAG, spot), self-clinching fasteners (PEM-type nuts, studs, standoffs), blind rivets, screws, clinching, adhesive. Details in `knowledge/14-welding-fasteners-finishing.md`.

docs.title: Sheet Metal Fundamentals (Sac Levha Temelleri)
docs.text:
Sheet Metal Fundamentals (Sac Levha Temelleri) › 9. Common failure patterns

1. Hole or cut-out too close to a bend → deformed feature.
2. No relief at the end of a bend → tearing and bulging.
3. Flat pattern generated with a K-factor that does not match the shop's process → parts too long/short after bending.
4. Dimensioning the bent part from the wrong side (inside vs outside) → accumulated error.
5. Using a thickness that is not stocked in the required grade.
6. Painting or powder-coating a surface that is also a gasket, grounding (earth bonding), or press-fit surface without masking.
7. Specifying a finish without specifying where the hanging marks may be.

docs.title: Sheet Metal Fundamentals (Sac Levha Temelleri)
docs.section: 10. What to ask when information is missing
docs.text:
Sheet Metal Fundamentals (Sac Levha Temelleri) › 10. What to ask when information is missing

Material and grade · thickness · quantity · process and machine · inside radius or tooling · K-factor or bend table source · finish · tolerance class · delivery form (DXF, STEP, drawing) · acceptance criteria.

docs.title: Bending and Flat Pattern (Büküm ve Açınım)
docs.text:
Bending and Flat Pattern (Büküm ve Açınım) › Overview

# Bending and Flat Pattern (Büküm ve Açınım)

docs.title: Bending and Flat Pattern (Büküm ve Açınım)
docs.text:
Bending and Flat Pattern (Büküm ve Açınım) › 1. Symbols

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| T | material thickness (mm) |
| R | **inside** bend radius (mm) |
| θ | bend angle = the angle the flange is turned through. A flat sheet is 0°; a right-angle bend is 90° |
| K | K-factor = distance of the neutral axis from the inside surface ÷ T |
| BA | bend allowance (bükme payı) |
| BD | bend deduction (bükme düşümü) |
| OSSB | outside setback |

Always state whether θ is the *turned* angle (90° for an L) or the *included* angle (also 90° for an L, but 45° turned vs 135° included for a shallow bend). For anything other than 90° this is the most common source of error.

docs.title: Bending and Flat Pattern (Büküm ve Açınım)
docs.text:
Bending and Flat Pattern (Büküm ve Açınım) › 2. Formulas

```text
BA   = θ[rad] × (R + K·T)            θ[rad] = θ[°] × π / 180
OSSB = (R + T) × tan(θ / 2)
BD   = 2 × OSSB − BA
```
- If flanges are dimensioned **outside to outside**:   `Flat length = Σ(outside flange lengths) − Σ(BD)`
- If dimensioned **to the bend tangent lines (inside/flat segments)**:   `Flat length = Σ(flat segments) + Σ(BA)`

docs.title: Bending and Flat Pattern (Büküm ve Açınım)
docs.text:
Bending and Flat Pattern (Büküm ve Açınım) › 3. K-factor is not a constant

K depends on material, thickness, radius, bending method (air bend, bottoming, coining), tooling and grain direction. Common textbook starting values for **air bending, mild steel** (use only when no shop data exists, and label the result as an estimate):

| R / T | Starting K (estimate) |
|---|---|
| < 1 | ≈ 0.33 |
| 1 – 3 | ≈ 0.38 – 0.42 |
| > 3 | ≈ 0.45 – 0.50 |

Stainless and hard aluminium alloys behave differently (more springback, different neutral-axis shift). The correct K is obtained from: (1) the fabricator's bend table, (2) a **test bend** (measure the flat length before and after), or (3) the supplier's published data.

docs.title: Bending and Flat Pattern (Büküm ve Açınım)
docs.text:
Bending and Flat Pattern (Büküm ve Açınım) › 4. Worked example A — single 90° bend

T = 2 mm, R = 2 mm, θ = 90°, K = 0.40, outside legs 50 mm and 30 mm.
- BA = (π/2) × (2 + 0.4×2) = **4.398 mm**
- OSSB = (2 + 2) × tan 45° = **4.000 mm**
- BD = 2×4.000 − 4.398 = **3.602 mm**
- Flat length = 50 + 30 − 3.602 = **76.398 mm**
Check by the second method: flat segments are 50 − 4 = 46 and 30 − 4 = 26 mm, so 46 + 26 + 4.398 = 76.398 mm ✓.

docs.title: Bending and Flat Pattern (Büküm ve Açınım)
docs.text:
Bending and Flat Pattern (Büküm ve Açınım) › 5. Worked example B — U-channel

T = 1.5 mm, R = 1.5 mm, K = 0.38, outside dimensions 20 / 60 / 20 mm, two 90° bends.
- BA = (π/2) × (1.5 + 0.38×1.5) = 3.252 mm; OSSB = 3.0 mm; BD = 6.0 − 3.252 = **2.748 mm** per bend.
- Flat length = 100 − 2×2.748 = **94.503 mm**.

docs.title: Bending and Flat Pattern (Büküm ve Açınım)
docs.text:
Bending and Flat Pattern (Büküm ve Açınım) › 6. Press brake basics (V-die air bending)

| Thickness T | Typical V-die opening (rule of thumb) |
|---|---|
| < 3 mm | ≈ 6 × T |
| 3 – 10 mm | ≈ 8 × T |
| 10 – 12 mm | ≈ 10 × T |
| > 12 mm | ≈ 12 × T |

- Minimum flange length (air bending) is about **0.7 × V** (V = 8 × 3 = 24 mm gives ≈ 17 mm for a 3 mm sheet). This is why 3 mm sheet with a 10 mm flange is a tooling problem.
- In air bending the inside radius is determined by the die opening (≈ 0.16 × V for mild steel), not by the punch tip. Specifying a radius that does not match any available V-die forces bottoming/coining or special tools.
- Bend force grows with T² / V and with material strength; stainless needs noticeably more than mild steel for the same geometry.
- Springback: expect a few degrees on stainless and high-strength steel; the machine compensates by over-bending, but part-to-part spread remains.
- Bend sequence: the last bends must not collide with the machine, the punch or the already formed flanges. Deep boxes need a gooseneck or special punches; U-shaped sections with narrow openings may be impossible to form in one piece.

docs.title: Bending and Flat Pattern (Büküm ve Açınım)
docs.text:
Bending and Flat Pattern (Büküm ve Açınım) › 7. Features near bends

Hole, slot or notch too close to a bend line → distorts. Use the distances in `01-sheet-metal-fundamentals.md` as a starting point; the safer alternative is to move the feature, add relief, or punch/laser it after bending (secondary operation, higher cost).

docs.title: Bending and Flat Pattern (Büküm ve Açınım)
docs.text:
Bending and Flat Pattern (Büküm ve Açınım) › 8. Reliefs and corners

- **Bend relief** (büküm boşaltması): small notch at the end of a bend to prevent tearing.
- **Corner relief** (köşe boşaltması): needed where two bends meet; closed corners need a gap (typically ≥ T) or weld/overlap definition.
- **Rip / yırtma**: a deliberate slit at a box corner so the flat blank can unfold.

docs.title: Bending and Flat Pattern (Büküm ve Açınım)
docs.text:
Bending and Flat Pattern (Büküm ve Açınım) › 9. Hems (kıvırma)

Open hem, closed hem (flattened), teardrop hem. Closed hems usually need a two-stage process (pre-bend at ~30° then flatten). The flat-length rule differs from a normal bend; use the shop's value or test.

docs.title: Bending and Flat Pattern (Büküm ve Açınım)
docs.text:
Bending and Flat Pattern (Büküm ve Açınım) › 10. Flat pattern checklist

1. Material, thickness, grade confirmed.
2. K-factor or bend table source identified and recorded **in the drawing note**.
3. All bends have direction (up/down), angle, radius.
4. Flat pattern bounding box compared with the expected sheet size.
5. Feature-to-bend distances checked.
6. Bend lines are on a separate layer in DXF (not cut).
7. A test part has been bent and measured before releasing a large series.

docs.title: Bending and Flat Pattern (Büküm ve Açınım)
docs.section: 11. What the AI must not do
docs.text:
Bending and Flat Pattern (Büküm ve Açınım) › 11. What the AI must not do

- Quote a K-factor as if it were a material constant.
- Give a bend radius as "standard" without naming the die and the shop.
- Present a calculated flat length as validated without a source for K.

docs.title: SolidWorks Sheet Metal Workflow
docs.text:
SolidWorks Sheet Metal Workflow › Overview

# SolidWorks Sheet Metal Workflow

**Version warning.** Command names, dialog layout and defaults change between SolidWorks releases and between language packs. This file uses the **English command names**. In a Turkish interface, look the command up with the command search box or the right-click menu, and use the label the user actually sees (see `04-solidworks-turkish-ui-and-terminology.md`). Never invent a menu path.

docs.title: SolidWorks Sheet Metal Workflow
docs.section: 1. Two ways to start a sheet-metal part
docs.text:
SolidWorks Sheet Metal Workflow › 1. Two ways to start a sheet-metal part

1. **Native sheet-metal modelling** — begin with *Base Flange/Tab* from a sketch (open or closed profile). The part gets a `Sheet-Metal` feature (holds default bend radius, thickness, K-factor/bend method, auto-relief) and a `Flat-Pattern` feature that is suppressed until you flatten.
2. **Convert a solid** — *Convert to Sheet Metal* (shell the solid first, choose the fixed face and bend edges, then add rips). Useful for imported geometry; needs clean, uniform wall thickness.

docs.title: SolidWorks Sheet Metal Workflow
docs.text:
SolidWorks Sheet Metal Workflow › 2. Core features (English names)

| Feature | Use |
|---|---|
| Base Flange/Tab | First wall; open sketch → bends are added automatically with the default radius |
| Edge Flange | Add a flange along an edge (angle, length convention, position, relief) |
| Miter Flange | Flanges along a sketched path with mitred corners |
| Hem | Open/closed/teardrop/rolled edge |
| Jog | Offset step in a flat wall |
| Sketched Bend | Bend along a sketched line in a flat region |
| Lofted-Bend | Transition between two profiles (cones, hoppers) |
| Closed Corner | Close the gap between two flanges at a corner |
| Break-Corner / Corner-Trim | Chamfer or round sheet corners |
| Forming Tool | Louvers, ribs, extrusions from the tool library |
| Vent | Grille/vent patterns |
| Rip | Open a sharp edge in a shell |
| Insert Bends | Convert a solid to sheet-metal bends |
| Unfold / Fold | Temporarily flatten selected bends to cut across them |
| Flatten (Flat-Pattern) | Toggle the full flat pattern |
| Normal Cut (option in Extruded Cut) | Cut perpendicular to the sheet through formed surfaces; needed for cuts across bends in a way that flattens correctly |

docs.title: SolidWorks Sheet Metal Workflow
docs.section: 3. Bend parameters — the settings that control flat-length
docs.text:
SolidWorks Sheet Metal Workflow › 3. Bend parameters — the settings that control flat-length

In the `Sheet-Metal` feature (and each flange) choose how the flat length is computed:
- **K-Factor** — enter the ratio.
- **Bend Allowance** — enter the length directly.
- **Bend Deduction** — enter the deduction directly.
- **Bend Table** — lookup file (Excel or text) by material, thickness, radius, angle.
- **Gauge table** — table of allowed thickness/radius combinations per material; applies thickness and radius automatically.

Key rule: **the CAD method must match the shop's process.** If the shop uses its own bend table, the same table has to be loaded in the SolidWorks file or the flat DXF will be wrong. Record the method in the drawing note (e.g. "Flat pattern generated with K = 0.40, ref. shop bend table rev. B").

docs.title: SolidWorks Sheet Metal Workflow
docs.text:
SolidWorks Sheet Metal Workflow › 4. Auto-relief and corners

Relief type options: **Rectangular, Obround, Tear**. Choose by process: tear relief is cheapest but leaves a sharp edge; rectangular and obround are cut by laser/punch. Relief ratio and corner treatment are part of the model, not an afterthought.

docs.title: SolidWorks Sheet Metal Workflow
docs.section: 5. Typical modelling sequence for an enclosure
docs.text:
SolidWorks Sheet Metal Workflow › 5. Typical modelling sequence for an enclosure

1. Define thickness, material, default radius, bend method (Sheet-Metal feature).
2. Base Flange/Tab (back panel) → Edge Flanges (sides) → Closed Corner / corner relief.
3. Hems and return flanges for stiffness and sealing faces.
4. Cuts: use Extruded Cut with *Normal Cut* for features crossing bends; add forming tools (louvers) from the library.
5. Add holes for hardware; confirm clearance holes vs PEM/clinch holes (different diameters).
6. Flatten; inspect for overlaps, self-intersection, relief and bend lines.
7. Check the bounding box against the sheet format.
8. Set custom properties (material, thickness, finish, weight, revision).
9. Create the drawing (flat pattern view + bent view) and the DXF.

docs.title: SolidWorks Sheet Metal Workflow
docs.text:
SolidWorks Sheet Metal Workflow › 6. Flat pattern and DXF export

- Right-click the `Flat-Pattern` feature (or use the export command) to export DXF/DWG. Export options include which entities (geometry, bend lines, forming tool markers, sketches) and the bend-line layer/linetype.
- **Cut geometry and bend lines must be separable** (different layer/colour) so the laser does not cut the bend lines. See `skills/solidworks-dxf-release-check`.
- Always open the DXF in a viewer or the CAM system before release; check units (mm), scale 1:1, no stray sketch geometry, no hidden duplicate lines.
- If the part contains forming tools, decide whether the DXF should include only the cut outline (usual for laser) or marking geometry.

docs.title: SolidWorks Sheet Metal Workflow
docs.section: 7. Common errors and what to check
docs.text:
SolidWorks Sheet Metal Workflow › 7. Common errors and what to check

| Symptom | Likely cause | Check |
|---|---|---|
| Flat-Pattern is red/fails to flatten | Overlap, missing relief, closed corner without gap, thickness inconsistency | Highlight the failing face in the error message; add relief; verify one fixed face |
| Bend lines missing in DXF | Export option off | Export options → bend lines |
| Flat length differs from shop result | Wrong K-factor / bend table | Compare with a test bend; align table |
| Cut across bends is distorted in flat | Cut made in folded state with perpendicular-to-face instead of Normal Cut | Use Normal Cut or unfold → cut → fold |
| Hole becomes oval in the flat | Hole is on a bend region | Move away from the bend; see distance rules |
| Imported STEP will not convert | Non-uniform thickness, fillets not matching | Rebuild as native sheet metal |

docs.title: SolidWorks Sheet Metal Workflow
docs.text:
SolidWorks Sheet Metal Workflow › 8. Custom properties and cut list

Useful part properties for release: material, thickness, finish, weight, revision, drawing number, part number. For sheet-metal parts the cut list can carry sheet-metal data (thickness, bounding box length/width, number of bends) — check the exact property names in the installed version because they differ between versions and languages.

SolidWorks Turkish Interface and Terminology › Overview

# SolidWorks Turkish Interface and Terminology

docs.title: SolidWorks Turkish Interface and Terminology
docs.text:
SolidWorks Turkish Interface and Terminology › 1. The honest status

The Turkish **UI labels** in this library are **not verified** against an installed Turkish SolidWorks. A made-up button name is worse than none, so the library treats labels in three confidence levels:

| Level | Meaning | How the AI writes it |
|---|---|---|
| **V** (verified) | Copied from a screenshot or text supplied by a user with the stated SolidWorks version | Use the Turkish label as shown |
| **C** (common) | Widely used core term, high confidence, still unverified for the specific version | Use it, add "(ekranda farklı görünebilir)" if the step matters |
| **U** (unverified) | Not checked | Write the English command name; put `[doğrulanmadı]` next to any Turkish guess |

Machine-readable file: `reference/solidworks-ui-labels.csv` (EN command, TR label, level, version, source, note). Anyone can fill it from screenshots.

docs.title: SolidWorks Turkish Interface and Terminology
docs.section: 2. Three layers that must never be mixed
docs.text:
SolidWorks Turkish Interface and Terminology › 2. Three layers that must never be mixed

1. **UI path** — what to click (language and version dependent).
2. **Feature / property name** — what appears in the FeatureManager tree or in custom properties (language dependent; a property created in a Turkish session keeps its Turkish name).
3. **API name** — macro/API identifiers are **always English** (`ModelDoc2`, `FeatureManager`, `CustomPropertyManager`).

docs.title: SolidWorks Turkish Interface and Terminology
docs.section: 3. Core terms with level C (confidence: common)
docs.text:
SolidWorks Turkish Interface and Terminology › 3. Core terms with level C (confidence: common)

| English | Turkish | Level |
|---|---|---|
| Part | Parça | C |
| Assembly | Montaj | C |
| Drawing | Teknik resim | C |
| Sketch | Eskiz | C |
| Feature / FeatureManager | Özellik / Özellik Yöneticisi | C |
| Dimension | Ölçü | C |
| Configuration | Konfigürasyon | C |
| Rebuild | Yeniden oluştur | U |
| Sheet metal | Sac levha | C (trade term); menu label U |
| Flat pattern | Açınım / Düz açınım | C (trade term); feature label U |

Everything else is U until verified. Do **not** extend this table without evidence.

docs.title: SolidWorks Turkish Interface and Terminology
docs.section: 4. How the AI should answer a SolidWorks question in Turkish
docs.text:
SolidWorks Turkish Interface and Terminology › 4. How the AI should answer a SolidWorks question in Turkish

1. Ask once for the **SolidWorks version** and whether the UI is Turkish.
2. Give the English command name first when the Turkish label is U: "**Edge Flange** (Kenar Flanşı olabilir — ekranda doğrula)".
3. Tell the user how to find the command without knowing the label: type the English or Turkish word in the command search box, or right-click the feature in the tree.
4. Offer a screenshot request when the label matters: "Menünün ekran görüntüsünü gönderirsen Türkçe adı kayda geçiririm."
5. Never write a menu path as if it were certain when it is U.

Example answer (U-level command):
> Sac levha parçada kenarı bükmek için **Edge Flange** komutunu kullan. Türkçe arayüzde adı sürüme göre değişebilir; komut arama kutusuna "flanş" veya "edge" yazarak bulabilirsin. Ekranda gördüğün adı yazarsan sonraki adımlarda onu kullanırım.

docs.title: SolidWorks Turkish Interface and Terminology
docs.section: 5. Capture protocol (how to verify labels quickly)
docs.text:
SolidWorks Turkish Interface and Terminology › 5. Capture protocol (how to verify labels quickly)

1. Open a Turkish SolidWorks; note the version (Help → About).
2. For each command: screenshot of the toolbar tooltip *and* of the PropertyManager title.
3. Fill one row in `reference/solidworks-ui-labels.csv`: `en_command, tr_label, level=V, version, source=screenshot, note`.
4. Run `python scripts/validate_reference.py` to check the CSV.
5. Re-run the evaluation set (`training/eval`) to confirm the AI uses V rows correctly.

docs.title: SolidWorks Turkish Interface and Terminology
docs.text:
SolidWorks Turkish Interface and Terminology › 6. Turkish technical writing policy (summary)

Order of preference: exact UI label → standard term → established shop term → Öztürkçe word where it is already in real use and unambiguous → coined words only as marked suggestions. Full rules: `docs/terminology-policy.md`. Glossary: `reference/glossary-sacmetal.md`.

docs.title: Sheet Metal Enclosures, IP and IK Ratings
docs.text:
Sheet Metal Enclosures, IP and IK Ratings › Overview

# Sheet Metal Enclosures, IP and IK Ratings (Sac Kabin, IP ve IK Sınıfları)

docs.title: Sheet Metal Enclosures, IP and IK Ratings
docs.text:
Sheet Metal Enclosures, IP and IK Ratings › 1. The golden rule

An **IP rating is earned by test, not by drawing.** A design can *target* a rating and a review can find leakage paths, but "this is IP65" is a statement that needs a test report (own lab, accredited lab, or the component supplier's type-test for a catalogue enclosure). The AI must never say "guaranteed IP65" from geometry.

docs.title: Sheet Metal Enclosures, IP and IK Ratings
docs.text:
Sheet Metal Enclosures, IP and IK Ratings › 2. IP code (IEC 60529 / EN 60529 / TS EN 60529)

Format: `IP` + first digit (solids) + second digit (water) + optional letters. `X` means "not rated for that part", e.g. `IPX4`.

**First digit — solid objects and dust**
| Digit | Protection |
|---|---|
| 0 | none |
| 1 | objects ≥ 50 mm |
| 2 | objects ≥ 12.5 mm (finger) |
| 3 | objects ≥ 2.5 mm |
| 4 | objects ≥ 1 mm |
| 5 | dust-protected (limited ingress, no harmful deposit) |
| 6 | dust-tight (no ingress, vacuum test) |

**Second digit — water**
| Digit | Protection |
|---|---|
| 0 | none |
| 1 | vertically dripping |
| 2 | dripping, enclosure tilted up to 15° |
| 3 | spraying up to 60° from vertical |
| 4 | splashing from any direction |
| 5 | water jets, 6.3 mm nozzle |
| 6 | powerful jets, 12.5 mm nozzle |
| 7 | temporary immersion (typically up to 1 m, 30 min) |
| 8 | continuous immersion, conditions agreed with manufacturer |
| 9 | high-pressure, high-temperature jets (IEC 60529 amendment; `IPX9K` in ISO 20653 for road vehicles) |

Important consequences
- IP65 does not imply IP64, IP66 or IP67 tests were passed. IP66 and IP67 do **not** include each other; a product that needs both is marked `IP66/IP67`.
- IP says nothing about corrosion, UV, impact, pressure, condensation, or explosion protection.
- The additional letters (A, B, C, D; H, M, S, W) are rarely used; do not add them without a source.

docs.title: Sheet Metal Enclosures, IP and IK Ratings
docs.text:
Sheet Metal Enclosures, IP and IK Ratings › 3. IK code (IEC 62262 / EN 50102 legacy)

Mechanical impact protection.
| IK | Impact energy |
|---|---|
| IK00 | not rated |
| IK01 | 0.14 J |
| IK02 | 0.2 J |
| IK03 | 0.35 J |
| IK04 | 0.5 J |
| IK05 | 0.7 J |
| IK06 | 1 J |
| IK07 | 2 J |
| IK08 | 5 J |
| IK09 | 10 J |
| IK10 | 20 J |
Sheet-metal enclosures often reach IK08–IK10 by wall thickness and construction, but windows, displays and plastic parts decide the real rating.

docs.title: Sheet Metal Enclosures, IP and IK Ratings
docs.text:
Sheet Metal Enclosures, IP and IK Ratings › 4. NEMA / UL types

NEMA 250 and UL 50/50E enclosure types (e.g. Type 4, 4X, 12) are **not one-to-one equivalent** to IP codes. They also include corrosion, icing, oil and other tests. Give a mapping only as "approximately comparable, not equivalent".

docs.title: Sheet Metal Enclosures, IP and IK Ratings
docs.section: 5. Leakage paths in a sheet-metal enclosure (checklist)
docs.text:
Sheet Metal Enclosures, IP and IK Ratings › 5. Leakage paths in a sheet-metal enclosure (checklist)

1. Door/cover seam — gasket continuity, corners, overlap.
2. Gasket joint (a gasket cut from strip is spliced; a moulded or foam-in-place gasket has no joint).
3. Welded seams — must be **continuous**; stitch or spot welds are not a seal.
4. Mounting holes — through-holes into the interior (rear panel holes) need sealing washers or blind (PEM/stud) fasteners.
5. Cable entries — glands, grommets, gland plates; **unused entries must be plugged**.
6. Windows and displays — gasket or adhesive seal; thermal expansion.
7. Vents/breathers — rating of the vent element; open louvers destroy IP5x/6x/ IPx4+.
8. Hinges, locks, handles — shaft seals; lock cut-outs.
9. Fastener screws on the gasket line — local stiffness and spacing.
10. Drains and condensation holes — deliberately open; they define the rating or must be a rated drain/breather.
11. Paint/powder on the gasket face — thickness, drips, runs, coating over welds.
12. Earth (ground) bonding points — masked paint surfaces create gaps if not sealed.

docs.title: Sheet Metal Enclosures, IP and IK Ratings
docs.section: 6. Design principles that matter in sheet metal
docs.text:
Sheet Metal Enclosures, IP and IK Ratings › 6. Design principles that matter in sheet metal

- **Door overlap / labyrinth**: a double-flanged (return) door edge helps against jets and rain; flat butt joints rely entirely on the gasket.
- **Roof slope / drip edge** for outdoor use; no flat top that collects water (IPx4 and above).
- **Gasket compression**: define the compression window from the gasket datasheet (often in the order of 20–40% for foam/elastomer, **verify**), then design the stop (hard stop, embossed stop, door-closing hardware) so that compression is *controlled*, not left to bolt torque.
- **Stiffness at the sealing line**: flanges should not bow between fasteners. Typical fastener pitch for a gasketed cover is shorter than for an unsealed cover (design check, not a rule).
- **Gasket groove vs flat gasket**: a groove controls compression and position; a flat gasket glued to the lid is cheaper but more sensitive to flatness.
- **Corners**: the most common leak; closed-corner welds must be ground flat or the gasket must run around a radius.
- **Cable glands**: use IP-rated glands matching the cable diameter range; the gland's own IP must be ≥ the enclosure's target; unused holes plugged.
- **Material compatibility**: gasket material vs UV, ozone, oil, temperature (EPDM, silicone, PU foam, neoprene differ). State environment.
- **Ventilation and thermal**: fan/filter and breathers are separate design topics; a closed IP65 enclosure traps heat; calculate the dissipated power and allowed internal temperature, consider heat exchanger/air-conditioner, or a rated breather element for pressure equalization.
- **Condensation**: breather membranes, anti-condensation heaters, drain; this is not part of the IP rating.

docs.title: Sheet Metal Enclosures, IP and IK Ratings
docs.text:
Sheet Metal Enclosures, IP and IK Ratings › 7. Related standards (where to look)

| Topic | Standard family |
|---|---|
| IP code | IEC 60529 (EN 60529) |
| IK code | IEC 62262 |
| Empty enclosures for low-voltage switchgear | IEC 62208 |
| Low-voltage switchgear and controlgear assemblies | IEC 61439 (EN 61439) |
| Machinery electrical equipment | IEC 60204-1 |
| North American enclosure types | NEMA 250, UL 50, UL 50E |
| Stainless/marine/chemical corrosion | project specification; ISO 12944 for coatings on steel structures |
Always cite edition and national adoption (TS EN ...) and confirm before quoting in a formal document.

docs.title: Sheet Metal Enclosures, IP and IK Ratings
docs.text:
Sheet Metal Enclosures, IP and IK Ratings › 8. Test and evidence

Distinguish: **design intent** (calculation, geometry review) → **prototype test** (own test with documented setup) → **accredited test report** (lab) → **declaration** in the product documentation. Warranty and certification language depends on which level exists.

docs.title: Sheet Metal Enclosures, IP and IK Ratings
docs.text:
Sheet Metal Enclosures, IP and IK Ratings › 9. Review output template

1. Target IP/IK and exposure (indoor/outdoor, wash-down, dust type, temperature, UV, chemicals).
2. List of leakage paths with a risk (low/medium/high) and a design response.
3. Open items (data needed: gasket datasheet, gland datasheet, cable list, heat load).
4. Test plan.
5. Statement of limits: "Target, not certified".

docs.title: Technical Drawing for Sheet Metal (Teknik Resim)
docs.text:
Technical Drawing for Sheet Metal (Teknik Resim) › Overview

# Technical Drawing for Sheet Metal (Teknik Resim)

docs.title: Technical Drawing for Sheet Metal (Teknik Resim)
docs.text:
Technical Drawing for Sheet Metal (Teknik Resim) › 1. Purpose

A drawing is a **contract**: it states what must be delivered and how it will be inspected. A model alone is not a contract unless the company works model-based (MBD) and agrees that.

docs.title: Technical Drawing for Sheet Metal (Teknik Resim)
docs.text:
Technical Drawing for Sheet Metal (Teknik Resim) › 2. Standards map (where to look)

| Question | Family |
|---|---|
| Line types, views, sections | ISO 128 series |
| Dimensioning principles | ISO 129-1 |
| Sheet sizes and layout | ISO 5457 |
| Title block | ISO 7200 |
| Scales | ISO 5455 |
| General tolerances | ISO 2768-1, ISO 2768-2 (replaced by ISO 22081 for geometrical general tolerances; check which your customer cites) |
| Geometrical tolerancing | ISO 1101; datums ISO 5459; ASME Y14.5 in US practice |
| Tolerancing principle | ISO 8015 (independence principle) |
| Surface texture | ISO 21920 series (older: ISO 1302 / ISO 4287) |
| Welding symbols | ISO 2553 |
| Welded structures general tolerance | ISO 13920 |
| Threads | ISO 6410 (representation), ISO 261/262 (metric) |
Verify the current edition before citing.

docs.title: Technical Drawing for Sheet Metal (Teknik Resim)
docs.text:
Technical Drawing for Sheet Metal (Teknik Resim) › 3. Sheet sizes and projection

A0 841×1189, A1 594×841, A2 420×594, A3 297×420, A4 210×297 (mm). Europe/Türkiye: **first-angle projection** (symbol: truncated cone, ISO). US: third angle. Always show the projection symbol.

docs.title: Technical Drawing for Sheet Metal (Teknik Resim)
docs.text:
Technical Drawing for Sheet Metal (Teknik Resim) › 4. Title block (minimum for release)

Part number · name · revision (with date and change description) · material and grade · thickness (sheet) · general tolerance note (e.g. ISO 2768-m) · surface finish/coating · scale · sheet size · units · projection symbol · drawn/checked/approved · company / confidentiality note · weight (if required) · mass tolerance if relevant. For sheet metal: "**flat pattern generated with K = … / bend table …**".

docs.title: Technical Drawing for Sheet Metal (Teknik Resim)
docs.section: 5. Views for a bent sheet-metal part
docs.text:
Technical Drawing for Sheet Metal (Teknik Resim) › 5. Views for a bent sheet-metal part

- Front/side/top views to define the **bent** shape.
- **Flat pattern view** (açınım) with overall flat dimensions and bend lines (direction, angle, radius).
- Detail and section views where needed.
- A 3D reference view is helpful but is not a dimension source.
- Bend table or bend notes: "BEND UP 90° R2" style, per bend, or a table with bend ID, direction, angle, inner radius.

docs.title: Technical Drawing for Sheet Metal (Teknik Resim)
docs.text:
Technical Drawing for Sheet Metal (Teknik Resim) › 6. Dimensioning rules

1. Each dimension once; no duplicates.
2. Do not make closed dimension chains (over-definition) — choose the functional chain.
3. State the convention for bent dimensions (to **outside** virtual sharp, to inside, or to mid-line). For sheet metal, "to outside virtual sharp" is common, but state it.
4. Dimension from datums that match the **inspection** and **assembly** method.
5. Holes: diameter, count, position from datums, tolerance only if functional; indicate PEM/clinch holes with part reference.
6. Radii: inside radius, thickness-based note acceptable.
7. Chamfers and countersinks: angle and diameter.
8. Do not dimension the flat pattern and the bent part from conflicting references.
9. Reference dimensions in brackets (REF).

docs.title: Technical Drawing for Sheet Metal (Teknik Resim)
docs.section: 7. Notes that belong on sheet-metal drawings
docs.text:
Technical Drawing for Sheet Metal (Teknik Resim) › 7. Notes that belong on sheet-metal drawings

- Material/grade and thickness tolerance reference.
- General tolerances.
- Deburr and break sharp edges (e.g. 0.2–0.5 mm; state if different).
- Grain direction (if relevant).
- Surface finish and where it must **not** be applied (gasket, ground contact).
- Welding symbols or note: seam type, length, continuous/intermittent.
- Inspection requirements, e.g. critical dimensions marked.
- Packaging/marking if applicable (laser etching).

docs.title: Technical Drawing for Sheet Metal (Teknik Resim)
docs.text:
Technical Drawing for Sheet Metal (Teknik Resim) › 8. Revision control

Every change → new revision letter/number, date, description, who approved. A drawing issued without a revision is not controllable. The BOM, the model and the DXF carry the same revision.

docs.title: Technical Drawing for Sheet Metal (Teknik Resim)
docs.text:
Technical Drawing for Sheet Metal (Teknik Resim) › 9. Review checklist (use as skill output)

Classify each finding as **Error** (blocks manufacture/inspection), **Risk** (ambiguous), **Suggestion**.
1. Title block complete? 2. Views sufficient? 3. Flat pattern present? 4. Dimension conflicts? 5. Tolerance statement present? 6. Datum scheme coherent? 7. Bend notes correct and matching count? 8. Finish and masking? 9. Material and thickness consistent with BOM/model? 10. Revision consistent across documents? 11. Values read from an image are flagged as "read from image".

docs.title: Technical Drawing for Sheet Metal (Teknik Resim)
docs.text:
Technical Drawing for Sheet Metal (Teknik Resim) › 10. Failure patterns

No general tolerance note · flat pattern missing · K-factor not stated · inside/outside mix · dimension chain closed · GD&T frame references an undefined datum · title-block material differs from the BOM · revision not updated after a model change · DXF shows bend lines as cut lines.

docs.title: GD&T and General Tolerances (Geometrik Toleranslandırma)
docs.text:
GD&T and General Tolerances (Geometrik Toleranslandırma) › Overview

# GD&T and General Tolerances (Geometrik Toleranslandırma)

docs.title: GD&T and General Tolerances (Geometrik Toleranslandırma)
docs.text:
GD&T and General Tolerances (Geometrik Toleranslandırma) › 1. Why GD&T

Plus/minus tolerances control a size but not its form, orientation or location relative to functional surfaces. GD&T states **function-based** requirements with datums that match how the part is assembled and inspected. Use it only where function demands it; sheet-metal parts are mostly controlled by general tolerances plus a few critical features.

docs.title: GD&T and General Tolerances (Geometrik Toleranslandırma)
docs.text:
GD&T and General Tolerances (Geometrik Toleranslandırma) › 2. Symbols (ISO 1101 geometrical characteristics)

| Type | Characteristic | Needs datum? | Typical sheet-metal use |
|---|---|---|---|
| Form | Straightness | No | Long edges, rails |
| Form | Flatness | No | Sealing face, mounting plate |
| Form | Circularity (roundness) | No | Rolled cylinders |
| Form | Cylindricity | No | Rolled/welded cylinders |
| Profile | Profile of a line | Optional | Cross-section of a formed section |
| Profile | Profile of a surface | Optional | Formed shape, cut contour |
| Orientation | Parallelism | Yes | Flange parallel to base |
| Orientation | Perpendicularity | Yes | Side wall to base |
| Orientation | Angularity | Yes | Non-90° flanges |
| Location | Position | Yes | Hole patterns, PEM holes |
| Location | Concentricity / Coaxiality | Yes | Rare in sheet metal |
| Location | Symmetry | Yes | Slots centered on a part |
| Run-out | Circular run-out | Yes | Rotating parts |
| Run-out | Total run-out | Yes | Rotating parts |
ISO 1101 lists concentricity and symmetry separately; ASME Y14.5 has not included concentricity and symmetry since the 2009 edition (position and profile are used instead). State which standard the drawing follows.

docs.title: GD&T and General Tolerances (Geometrik Toleranslandırma)
docs.text:
GD&T and General Tolerances (Geometrik Toleranslandırma) › 3. Feature control frame

`| symbol | ⌀ tolerance value + modifier | datum A | datum B | datum C |`
- A ⌀ in front of the value means a cylindrical tolerance zone (hole position).
- Modifiers: Ⓜ maximum material condition (MMC), Ⓛ least material condition (LMC), Ⓟ projected tolerance zone, Ⓕ free state (non-rigid parts, relevant for thin sheet metal). Use only if the function (assembly clearance) justifies it.
- Datum order matters: primary (3 points of contact), secondary (2), tertiary (1).

docs.title: GD&T and General Tolerances (Geometrik Toleranslandırma)
docs.text:
GD&T and General Tolerances (Geometrik Toleranslandırma) › 4. Datum strategy for sheet metal

- The datum surfaces should be **stable and reachable**: a flat mounting face, a large flange, a pattern of holes.
- Avoid datums on bent corner radii or on thin unsupported flanges.
- A thin sheet is non-rigid: state the **restraint condition** in the note (e.g. ISO 10579 non-rigid parts), or the part will measure differently on every fixture.
- Choose datums to match assembly: the face that touches the mounting surface is datum A; hole pattern for fasteners is the location reference (B, C).

docs.title: GD&T and General Tolerances (Geometrik Toleranslandırma)
docs.section: 5. Selection guide (what to control and how)
docs.text:
GD&T and General Tolerances (Geometrik Toleranslandırma) › 5. Selection guide (what to control and how)

| Requirement | Control |
|---|---|
| Mounting face must be flat | Flatness (e.g. 0.3 mm) |
| Door flange must be parallel to the frame | Parallelism to datum A |
| Hole pattern fits a mating part | Position of holes, ⌀ zone, with MMC if clearance holes |
| Slot centered on edge | Symmetry (ISO) or position (ASME) |
| Contour of a formed part | Profile of a surface |
| Side wall square to base | Perpendicularity |
Do not mix many controls on one feature without need; every frame adds inspection cost.

docs.title: GD&T and General Tolerances (Geometrik Toleranslandırma)
docs.text:
GD&T and General Tolerances (Geometrik Toleranslandırma) › 6. ISO 2768-1 general tolerances (linear dimensions, mm)

| Nominal range | f (fine) | m (medium) | c (coarse) | v (very coarse) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.5 – 3 | ±0.05 | ±0.1 | ±0.2 | — |
| > 3 – 6 | ±0.05 | ±0.1 | ±0.3 | ±0.5 |
| > 6 – 30 | ±0.1 | ±0.2 | ±0.5 | ±1 |
| > 30 – 120 | ±0.15 | ±0.3 | ±0.8 | ±1.5 |
| > 120 – 400 | ±0.2 | ±0.5 | ±1.2 | ±2.5 |
| > 400 – 1000 | ±0.3 | ±0.8 | ±2 | ±4 |
| > 1000 – 2000 | ±0.5 | ±1.2 | ±3 | ±6 |
| > 2000 – 4000 | — | ±2 | ±4 | ±8 |

Angular tolerance by length of the shorter leg:
| Length (mm) | f / m | c | v |
|---|---|---|---|
| up to 10 | ±1° | ±1°30′ | ±3° |
| > 10 – 50 | ±0°30′ | ±1° | ±2° |
| > 50 – 120 | ±0°20′ | ±0°30′ | ±1° |
| > 120 – 400 | ±0°10′ | ±0°15′ | ±0°30′ |
| > 400 | ±0°5′ | ±0°10′ | ±0°20′ |

For sheet-metal bent parts, class **m** is the usual default; the achievable bend angle (±0.5°–1°) and leg length depend on process. A class **f** requirement across bends is typically unrealistic. A drawing written "ISO 2768-mK" refers to linear (m) and geometrical (K, from ISO 2768-2). ISO 22081 has since replaced ISO 2768-2 for geometrical general tolerances; verify which one the customer cites.

docs.title: GD&T and General Tolerances (Geometrik Toleranslandırma)
docs.text:
GD&T and General Tolerances (Geometrik Toleranslandırma) › 7. Fits (shaft/hole) — only a pointer

ISO 286 (IT grades and fit letters such as H7/g6) applies to machined features; sheet-metal holes are normally governed by general tolerance or an IT-class stated on the drawing (laser holes seldom reach IT8 without secondary operations).

docs.title: GD&T and General Tolerances (Geometrik Toleranslandırma)
docs.text:
GD&T and General Tolerances (Geometrik Toleranslandırma) › 8. How to avoid over-tolerancing

1. State the function. 2. Choose the loosest tolerance that works. 3. Check against the process capability (laser ±0.1–0.2, bend ±0.5°). 4. Check that the inspection method exists (CMM, gauge, optical). 5. Remove the tolerance if no function requires it.

docs.title: GD&T and General Tolerances (Geometrik Toleranslandırma)
docs.text:
GD&T and General Tolerances (Geometrik Toleranslandırma) › 9. Common GD&T mistakes

Datums not defined on the drawing · datum on a feature that moves · position tolerance relative to a free-form edge · missing datum order · ⌀ missing on a hole pattern · tolerance tighter than the manufacturing process · MMC without a clearance check · flatness tighter than the size tolerance allows.

docs.title: Estimating Dimensions from Images (Görselden Ölçü Tahmini)
docs.text:
Estimating Dimensions from Images (Görselden Ölçü Tahmini) › Overview

# Estimating Dimensions from Images (Görselden Ölçü Tahmini)

docs.title: Estimating Dimensions from Images (Görselden Ölçü Tahmini)
docs.section: 1. What is possible and what is not
docs.text:
Estimating Dimensions from Images (Görselden Ölçü Tahmini) › 1. What is possible and what is not

A photograph can give a **scale-based estimate** with an uncertainty. It cannot give a manufacturing dimension. Every number from an image must be labelled **estimate (from image)** with an error range and a confidence level. If the part will be manufactured, measure it physically (caliper, tape, CMM, 3D scan).

docs.title: Estimating Dimensions from Images (Görselden Ölçü Tahmini)
docs.text:
Estimating Dimensions from Images (Görselden Ölçü Tahmini) › 2. Methods, from best to weakest

| Method | Requirement | Typical error |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Reference object in the same plane** (ruler, A4 sheet, coin, known standard part) | Plane of the object parallel to the camera; reference in the same plane | ~1–3 % when done carefully |
| **B. Known feature of the part** (standard hole, M8 nut, DIN rail width, 19" rack unit) | The feature size is certain | 2–5 % |
| **C. Perspective correction (homography)** using four known points of a rectangle | Four coplanar points, known rectangle size | 1–3 % in the plane |
| **D. Pinhole camera model** `Z = f·H/h` | Known focal length, sensor size, distance | 5–15 %; distance error dominates |
| **E. Multiple views / photogrammetry** | Many overlapping photos + scale bar | ~0.1–1 % with a good setup |
| **F. Visual guess without reference** | none | **Not acceptable as a result**; give a range and say so |

docs.title: Estimating Dimensions from Images (Görselden Ölçü Tahmini)
docs.text:
Estimating Dimensions from Images (Görselden Ölçü Tahmini) › 3. Core formulas

Scale (method A): `mm_per_pixel = L_ref[mm] / L_ref[px]`;  `L_obj = L_obj[px] × mm_per_pixel`.
Example: an A4 sheet's long side (297 mm) measures 1485 px; the part measures 640 px → 0.2 mm/px → **128 mm**.
Error propagation (relative errors add roughly): if each pixel measurement has ±3 px: `δ ≈ L × (3/1485 + 3/640) ≈ 0.67 %` → ±0.86 mm for 128 mm — the **pixel** error is small; the real error is dominated by perspective and plane mismatch, usually several times larger. Always add a plane/perspective error term.
Pinhole (method D): `Z = f × H / h` where f is the focal length in the same unit as h (convert pixels with sensor pixel size: `pixel_size = sensor_width / image_width_px`).
Depth difference: an object closer to the camera than the reference looks larger; a feature 10 % closer appears ~10 % larger. **Reference and measured feature must be at the same distance.**

docs.title: Estimating Dimensions from Images (Görselden Ölçü Tahmini)
docs.text:
Estimating Dimensions from Images (Görselden Ölçü Tahmini) › 4. Photographing for measurement (protocol)

1. Camera perpendicular to the measured plane; part centered; avoid wide-angle lenses and phone ultra-wide mode (distortion).
2. Put the reference object **next to the part, in the same plane**; flat, unfolded.
3. Ruler/scale visible along both axes if possible.
4. Same distance for reference and part; no zoom change between shots.
5. Even light; no strong shadows on edges.
6. Take 2–3 photos; keep the original file (not a cropped screenshot).
7. Provide: material, thickness (if known), what is the function of the part.

docs.title: Estimating Dimensions from Images (Görselden Ölçü Tahmini)
docs.text:
Estimating Dimensions from Images (Görselden Ölçü Tahmini) › 5. Typical error sources

Perspective / camera not perpendicular · lens distortion at the image edges · reference not in the same plane · low resolution (few pixels per mm) · edge blur · compression artifacts · shadows interpreted as edges · reference with unknown real size (a "credit card" is 85.60 × 53.98 mm; A4 is 210 × 297 mm; coins differ between countries).

docs.title: Estimating Dimensions from Images (Görselden Ölçü Tahmini)
docs.text:
Estimating Dimensions from Images (Görselden Ölçü Tahmini) › 6. Handling sheet-metal parts

- Flat blank (plaka): good for contour estimate, hole positions, overall size.
- Bent part: only projected dimensions in the plane; bend radii and angles need a profile view.
- Thickness: from an edge-on photo with a reference or caliper; an image can tell "about 2 mm", not "1.5 vs 2".
- Hole diameters: measure against a reference at the same plane.
- Reconstructing a flat pattern from a bent photo is possible only with additional bend data; flag as concept.

docs.title: Estimating Dimensions from Images (Görselden Ölçü Tahmini)
docs.section: 7. Report format (what the AI must return)
docs.text:
Estimating Dimensions from Images (Görselden Ölçü Tahmini) › 7. Report format (what the AI must return)

| Item | Estimated value | Error range | Confidence (low/med/high) | Method / reference used |
|---|---|---|---|---|
Followed by: assumptions (plane parallel? reference size certain?), what to measure physically, and the statement "estimate from image — not for manufacturing".

docs.title: Estimating Dimensions from Images (Görselden Ölçü Tahmini)
docs.text:
Estimating Dimensions from Images (Görselden Ölçü Tahmini) › 8. Refusal conditions

No reference object and no known feature → give relative proportions only. Reference at a different distance → say so and give a wider range. Blurry/low-resolution image → list which values could not be read.

docs.title: CAD Engineering Practice (CAD Mühendislik Pratiği)
docs.text:
CAD Engineering Practice (CAD Mühendislik Pratiği) › Overview

# CAD Engineering Practice (CAD Mühendislik Pratiği)

docs.title: CAD Engineering Practice (CAD Mühendislik Pratiği)
docs.section: 1. File formats and what each is for
docs.text:
CAD Engineering Practice (CAD Mühendislik Pratiği) › 1. File formats and what each is for

| Format | Use | Pitfall |
|---|---|---|
| Native (SLDPRT, SLDASM, SLDDRW) | Design work | Needs the same CAD and often the same version; references break when files move |
| STEP (.stp/.step, AP203/214/242) | Neutral 3D exchange | No feature tree; check units; configurations are not preserved |
| Parasolid (.x_t/.x_b) | Exchange between Parasolid-based CAD | Version limits |
| IGES | Legacy surface exchange | Stitching problems; avoid for solids |
| DXF / DWG | 2D profiles for laser/punch, drawings exchange | Units, layers, splines, scale, bend lines |
| PDF | Released drawing | Not a data source; vector PDF preferred over scan |
| STL / 3MF | 3D printing, visualisation | Mesh only |
| 3D PDF / eDrawings | Review | Not for manufacturing data |
Rule: release **drawing PDF + DXF (flat) + STEP (3D)** with the same revision label.

docs.title: CAD Engineering Practice (CAD Mühendislik Pratiği)
docs.text:
CAD Engineering Practice (CAD Mühendislik Pratiği) › 2. Naming and numbering

Part numbers are meaningful identifiers, not descriptions. Keep the number short, unique, immutable; put description in the properties. File name = part number + revision only if the PDM does not manage revisions. Avoid spaces, Turkish characters (ç, ğ, ı, ö, ş, ü) and special characters in file names exchanged with other systems, to avoid encoding problems.

docs.title: CAD Engineering Practice (CAD Mühendislik Pratiği)
docs.text:
CAD Engineering Practice (CAD Mühendislik Pratiği) › 3. Folder and reference hygiene

- One project folder, relative references, no local-drive links.
- Use **Pack and Go** (or the CAD's equivalent) for sending a complete assembly.
- Do not rename a file outside the CAD; use the CAD's rename or PDM so references update.
- Library parts (standard hardware) come from a controlled library, not a copy per project.

docs.title: CAD Engineering Practice (CAD Mühendislik Pratiği)
docs.text:
CAD Engineering Practice (CAD Mühendislik Pratiği) › 3b. Revision and change control

Revision in the title block, the model's properties and the file/PDM label must agree. A change requires: reason, scope, affected parts/drawings, approval, date. Keep the previous revision accessible (archive), never overwrite released files silently.

docs.title: CAD Engineering Practice (CAD Mühendislik Pratiği)
docs.text:
CAD Engineering Practice (CAD Mühendislik Pratiği) › 4. Modelling practice

1. Sketches fully defined; limit sketch complexity.
2. Capture design intent with a few master sketches/parameters/global variables rather than hundreds of ad-hoc dimensions.
3. Name important features and dimensions.
4. Use configurations/design tables for variants (sizes) instead of copies.
5. Keep assemblies mate-clean: fix the first component, avoid over-mated assemblies, use sub-assemblies to reflect real build structure.
6. Use lightweight/large-assembly modes on big assemblies; avoid circular references.
7. Check interference and clearance before release.
8. Keep units consistent (mm-g-s; or per company standard). Confirm the unit on imported files.

docs.title: CAD Engineering Practice (CAD Mühendislik Pratiği)
docs.section: 5. Release package for a sheet-metal part
docs.text:
CAD Engineering Practice (CAD Mühendislik Pratiği) › 5. Release package for a sheet-metal part

| Item | Check |
|---|---|
| 3D model | Material, thickness, mass |
| Drawing PDF | Revision, general tolerances, flat pattern, finish |
| DXF | Units mm, 1:1, bend lines separable, no stray geometry |
| BOM | Quantity, material, revision |
| Notes for quote | Quantity, finish, tolerances, delivery date |
| Change record | What changed since last revision |

docs.title: CAD Engineering Practice (CAD Mühendislik Pratiği)
docs.text:
CAD Engineering Practice (CAD Mühendislik Pratiği) › 6. Mass properties

Mass = volume × density; density comes from the material assigned in CAD and must match the real grade (e.g. 1.4301 ≈ 7900–8000 kg/m³, DC01 ≈ 7850 kg/m³, EN AW-5754 ≈ 2670 kg/m³). Coatings, welds, hardware and cut-outs affect the real mass. Mass in a CAD model is a *calculated* value; label it so.

docs.title: CAD Engineering Practice (CAD Mühendislik Pratiği)
docs.text:
CAD Engineering Practice (CAD Mühendislik Pratiği) › 7. Model-based definition (MBD) in short

Product and manufacturing information (PMI) attached to the 3D model can replace drawings **only** if the customer and quality system accept it. Otherwise keep the 2D drawing as the contractual document.

docs.title: CAD Engineering Practice (CAD Mühendislik Pratiği)
docs.text:
CAD Engineering Practice (CAD Mühendislik Pratiği) › 8. Handling of imported geometry

Check units and scale; check for gaps/sliver faces; heal faces; verify sheet thickness; rebuild as native sheet-metal when it will be flattened; do not trust an imported model's flatten result without a thickness check.

docs.title: CAD Engineering Practice (CAD Mühendislik Pratiği)
docs.text:
CAD Engineering Practice (CAD Mühendislik Pratiği) › 9. Data security

Customer drawings and models are confidential. Do not paste them into public tools; use approved environments (see `training/DATA-GOVERNANCE.md`).

docs.title: Technical and Engineering Documentation (Teknik Doküman Üretimi)
docs.text:
Technical and Engineering Documentation (Teknik Doküman Üretimi) › Overview

# Technical and Engineering Documentation (Teknik Doküman Üretimi)

docs.title: Technical and Engineering Documentation (Teknik Doküman Üretimi)
docs.text:
Technical and Engineering Documentation (Teknik Doküman Üretimi) › 1. Principles

1. **One purpose per document.** A reader should know in the first lines what the document is for and what to do with it.
2. **Facts, calculations, assumptions and open items are separated** (see the evidence labels below).
3. **Traceable**: document number, revision, date, author, approval, referenced drawings/standards with edition.
4. **Reproducible**: another engineer can repeat the calculation from the stated inputs.
5. **No invented data.** Missing information appears as an explicit "OPEN ITEM", never as a plausible number.

Evidence labels used everywhere in this library: `[FACT-SUPPLIED]`, `[CALCULATED]`, `[SOURCE-BACKED]`, `[PRACTICE]` (engineering practice), `[ESTIMATE]`, `[ASSUMPTION]`, `[OPEN]`.

docs.title: Technical and Engineering Documentation (Teknik Doküman Üretimi)
docs.text:
Technical and Engineering Documentation (Teknik Doküman Üretimi) › 2. Document types and minimum content

| Document | Purpose | Minimum sections |
|---|---|---|
| Design description (tasarım tanımı) | Explain a design for review | Scope, requirements, concept, key calculations, risks, open items |
| Technical specification (teknik şartname) | Define requirements for a supplier | Scope, normative references, requirements (shall/should), acceptance, deliverables |
| Datasheet (teknik veri föyü) | Product facts | Identification, dimensions, materials, ratings, environment, weight, standards |
| Work instruction (iş talimatı) | Perform a task consistently | Purpose, scope, tools/PPE, steps (numbered), checks, records |
| Inspection plan / report (muayene) | Prove conformity | Item, requirement, method, instrument, result, accept/reject, signature |
| Assembly instruction (montaj talimatı) | Build a product | Parts list, torque values, sequence, drawings |
| Test procedure / report (deney) | Verify a requirement | Objective, setup, pass criteria, steps, results, deviations |
| FAT/SAT (fabrika/saha kabul testi) | Customer acceptance | Test list, criteria, witnesses, punch list |
| User/maintenance manual | Safe use and service | Safety, transport, installation, operation, maintenance, spare parts |
| Calculation note (hesap föyü) | Support a decision | Inputs, method, formulas, results, checks, conclusion |
| BOM / cut list | What to buy/cut | Item, description, material, quantity, revision |
| Quotation technical annex | Scope of supply | Included, excluded, assumptions, drawings, delivery |

docs.title: Technical and Engineering Documentation (Teknik Doküman Üretimi)
docs.text:
Technical and Engineering Documentation (Teknik Doküman Üretimi) › 3. Requirement language

`shall` = mandatory; `should` = recommended; `may` = permitted. Each requirement has an identifier and is verifiable (a test, inspection or document check). "Fast", "robust", "sufficient" are not requirements.

docs.title: Technical and Engineering Documentation (Teknik Doküman Üretimi)
docs.section: 4. Writing style for Turkish engineering documents
docs.text:
Technical and Engineering Documentation (Teknik Doküman Üretimi) › 4. Writing style for Turkish engineering documents

- Short sentences; one instruction per step; imperative mood in procedures ("Parçayı sabitleyin.").
- Use the established term the reader knows; give the English term once in brackets when it helps.
- Consistent units (mm, kg, N·m); numbers with units; decimal comma or point consistent in the whole document (Turkish documents normally use a decimal comma; **state the convention when the document goes abroad**).
- Do not use vague words ("yaklaşık", "uygun") without a value or range.
- Tables for parameters; numbered steps for procedures; diagrams referenced by number.

docs.title: Technical and Engineering Documentation (Teknik Doküman Üretimi)
docs.text:
Technical and Engineering Documentation (Teknik Doküman Üretimi) › 5. Standard document skeleton

```text
Title · Document no. · Revision · Date · Author / Reviewer / Approver
1 Purpose and scope
2 Definitions and references (with edition)
3 Inputs and assumptions
4 Method / description
5 Results
6 Verification and checks
7 Open items and risks
8 Revision history
```

docs.title: Technical and Engineering Documentation (Teknik Doküman Üretimi)
docs.text:
Technical and Engineering Documentation (Teknik Doküman Üretimi) › 6. Calculation notes

Show the governing formula, the symbols, the units, the input values with source, the result with the number of significant digits that the inputs justify, and the check (order of magnitude, alternative method). Example format:

> **Weight of plate** `m = L·W·T·ρ = 1.0 × 2.0 × 0.003 m³ × 7850 kg/m³ = 47.1 kg` [CALCULATED] — density from the material certificate/standard [SOURCE-BACKED]; cutting, hardware and coating not included [ASSUMPTION].

docs.title: Technical and Engineering Documentation (Teknik Doküman Üretimi)
docs.text:
Technical and Engineering Documentation (Teknik Doküman Üretimi) › 7. Review checklist

Numbers consistent between text, tables and drawings · units · references with edition · revision history · all open items listed · no confidential data of other customers · spelling of part numbers · pagination and document number on every page.

docs.title: Technical and Engineering Documentation (Teknik Doküman Üretimi)
docs.text:
Technical and Engineering Documentation (Teknik Doküman Üretimi) › 8. AI behaviour for document generation

1. Ask for audience, purpose, language, and template if the document is formal.
2. Produce a **skeleton first** for long documents; confirm, then fill.
3. Insert `[OPEN]` for any missing mandatory data.
4. Never fabricate standard clauses, test results, signatures, certificate numbers or customer names.
5. For Word/PDF output: follow the file-creation procedures of the runtime; keep the content source in Markdown so that revisions are diffable.

docs.title: Quotation and Commercial Documents (Teklif Dokümanı)
docs.text:
Quotation and Commercial Documents (Teklif Dokümanı) › Overview

# Quotation and Commercial Documents (Teklif Dokümanı)

> This file is practical guidance, not legal or tax advice. Tax rates, legal terms and contract wording must be checked with the company's finance/legal staff.

docs.title: Quotation and Commercial Documents (Teklif Dokümanı)
docs.text:
Quotation and Commercial Documents (Teklif Dokümanı) › 1. What a good quotation does

It makes the buyer's decision easy and protects the seller from misunderstanding: what is included, what is not, at what price, until when, under which conditions.

docs.title: Quotation and Commercial Documents (Teklif Dokümanı)
docs.text:
Quotation and Commercial Documents (Teklif Dokümanı) › 2. Structure

1. Header: company, quotation number, date, validity period, revision, contact person.
2. Customer details and reference (RFQ number, drawing numbers, revisions).
3. **Scope of supply** — per item: description, drawing/part number + revision, material and thickness, finish, quantity.
4. **Price table** — unit price, quantity, line total, currency, price basis (per piece / per lot), tooling or one-off costs listed separately.
5. **Assumptions and exclusions** — e.g. "material price valid for order within X days", "tolerances per ISO 2768-m", "finish colour RAL ...", "no testing included", "transport excluded".
6. **Commercial terms** — delivery time (from order/from drawing approval/from material receipt), Incoterms 2020 term and named place, payment terms, validity, tax treatment, warranty, packaging, minimum order quantity.
7. **Technical annex** — drawings, flat patterns, tolerances, inspection and certificates (3.1 etc.) if requested.
8. Revision history and approval.

docs.title: Quotation and Commercial Documents (Teklif Dokümanı)
docs.text:
Quotation and Commercial Documents (Teklif Dokümanı) › 3. Pricing logic (see `12-cost-analysis.md`)

Quote price = **cost** + **margin** (state which: *markup on cost* or *margin on price* — they are different: a 20 % markup is a 16.7 % margin). Consider quantity breaks (setup amortisation), material volatility (price validity window or surcharge clause), and risk items (new process, tight tolerance).

docs.title: Quotation and Commercial Documents (Teklif Dokümanı)
docs.text:
Quotation and Commercial Documents (Teklif Dokümanı) › 4. Incoterms 2020 (short)

EXW (ex works), FCA (free carrier), CPT, CIP, DAP (delivered at place), DPU, DDP (delivered duty paid) for any mode; FAS, FOB, CFR, CIF for sea/inland waterway only. State the term **with a named place**, e.g. "DAP Istanbul". Confirm the current edition.

docs.title: Quotation and Commercial Documents (Teklif Dokümanı)
docs.text:
Quotation and Commercial Documents (Teklif Dokümanı) › 5. Tax and currency notes (Türkiye)

- VAT (KDV) rate and exemptions depend on the product, customer and current law; **check the current rate before issuing**. Write prices "KDV hariç" (excl. VAT) unless the company policy says otherwise.
- Currency: state it; for long validity add an exchange-rate clause (rate at invoice date or a fixed rate up to a date).
- Export: tax treatment differs; check with finance.

docs.title: Quotation and Commercial Documents (Teklif Dokümanı)
docs.section: 6. Typical commercial clauses (examples, not legal text)
docs.text:
Quotation and Commercial Documents (Teklif Dokümanı) › 6. Typical commercial clauses (examples, not legal text)

- Validity: "Bu teklif düzenleme tarihinden itibaren 15 gün geçerlidir." (set according to material volatility)
- Payment: advance %, balance on delivery, or net X days.
- Changes: drawings changes after order → price and lead-time review.
- Tolerance of quantity: ±x % for coated or nested production if agreed.
- Intellectual property: customer drawings remain customer property.

docs.title: Quotation and Commercial Documents (Teklif Dokümanı)
docs.section: 7. Risk and clarification list before quoting
docs.text:
Quotation and Commercial Documents (Teklif Dokümanı) › 7. Risk and clarification list before quoting

Missing drawing revision · conflicting material/thickness · unclear finish spec · tolerances tighter than process capability · unspecified annual volume · inspection and certificate requirements · packaging and logistics · penalty clauses. Convert them to **questions to the customer**, not silent assumptions.

docs.title: Quotation and Commercial Documents (Teklif Dokümanı)
docs.text:
Quotation and Commercial Documents (Teklif Dokümanı) › 8. Email cover template (Turkish)

> Konu: Teklif No TKL-XXXX – [Parça/Proje adı]
> Merhaba [Ad Soyad],
> [RFQ/Resim no]'ya istinaden teklifimizi ekte sunuyoruz. Teklif; [kapsam özeti] kalemlerini, [teslim süresi] teslim süresini ve [geçerlilik] geçerlilik süresini içermektedir. Varsayımlar ve hariç tutulan kalemler teklifin 5. bölümünde belirtilmiştir. Çizim revizyonu [Rev X] baz alınmıştır.
> Sorularınız için bana ulaşabilirsiniz.
> Saygılarımla,

docs.title: Quotation and Commercial Documents (Teklif Dokümanı)
docs.text:
Quotation and Commercial Documents (Teklif Dokümanı) › 9. AI behaviour

1. Ask for: items, quantities, drawings, material, finish, delivery, payment, validity, currency.
2. Pull prices only from supplied data or a stated cost model; mark rates as **illustrative** if they are not supplied.
3. Never invent customer names, prior orders, certifications or legal clauses.
4. Provide the quotation as a structured table first, then the narrative text.
5. List **assumptions and exclusions** every time.

docs.title: Sheet-Metal Cost Analysis (Maliyet Analizi)
docs.text:
Sheet-Metal Cost Analysis (Maliyet Analizi) › Overview

# Sheet-Metal Cost Analysis (Maliyet Analizi)

docs.title: Sheet-Metal Cost Analysis (Maliyet Analizi)
docs.text:
Sheet-Metal Cost Analysis (Maliyet Analizi) › 1. Cost model

```text
Part cost = Material + Cutting + Forming (bending) + Joining + Finishing + Hardware
          + Setup/Tooling (amortised) + Inspection + Packaging + Logistics
          + Overhead (genel gider) + Risk allowance
Price     = Cost + Margin
```
All rates in this file are **illustrative, not market data**. Replace them with the shop's numbers.

docs.title: Sheet-Metal Cost Analysis (Maliyet Analizi)
docs.text:
Sheet-Metal Cost Analysis (Maliyet Analizi) › 2. Components and drivers

| Component | Formula / driver |
|---|---|
| Material | `mass / nesting yield × price per kg`; mass = `L·W·T·ρ` of the **blank**, not the finished part |
| Nesting yield | usable-sheet utilisation; small parts in big sheets 70–85 %, depends on nesting and remnants |
| Laser cutting | `(cut length / cutting speed + pierces × pierce time) × machine rate`; speed falls with thickness |
| Punching | hits × time per hit × machine rate (+ tool cost if new tools) |
| Bending | `setup / batch + bends × handling time × press brake rate`; setup depends on tooling changes |
| Welding | length or number of tacks × time × rate; grinding after welding |
| Hardware (PEM, nuts, glands, gaskets) | purchase price × quantity + insertion time |
| Finishing | powder coat: area × price per m² (+ masking); galvanizing/anodizing: per kg or per m²; minimum lot charges |
| Inspection | frequency, first-article, certificate requirements |
| Packaging/logistics | per part or per pallet |
| Overhead | percent of direct cost or hourly burden |
| Risk | allowance for new process, tight tolerance, scrap risk |

docs.title: Sheet-Metal Cost Analysis (Maliyet Analizi)
docs.text:
Sheet-Metal Cost Analysis (Maliyet Analizi) › 3. Worked example (illustrative rates)

Part: flat blank 300 × 200 mm, 2 mm DC01, 4 holes ⌀10, 2 bends, powder coat, batch 50.
| Item | Calculation | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Mass of blank | 0.300 × 0.200 × 0.002 × 7850 | 0.942 kg |
| Material | 0.942 / 0.75 yield × 40 per kg | 50.24 |
| Cut length | 2×(300+200) + 4×π×10 | 1125.7 mm |
| Laser | (1125.7/2000 + 5 pierces × 0.5 s) × 30 per min | 18.13 |
| Bend setup | 30 min × 24 per min / 50 | 14.40 |
| Bend handling | 2 bends × 0.3 min × 24 | 14.40 |
| Powder coat | 0.12 m² (both faces) × 150 per m² | 18.00 |
| Packaging | — | 3.00 |
| **Direct cost** | | **118.17** |
| Overhead 12 % | | 14.18 |
| **Cost** | | **132.36** |
| Price with 20 % **markup on cost** | cost × 1.20 | 158.83 (margin on price 16.7 %) |
| Price for 20 % **margin on price** | cost / 0.80 (rounded cost 132.36) | 165.45 |

Batch sensitivity of the same part (same rates): batch 10 → cost 196.87; batch 50 → 132.36; batch 200 → 120.26. Setup amortisation is the largest lever on small batches.

docs.title: Sheet-Metal Cost Analysis (Maliyet Analizi)
docs.text:
Sheet-Metal Cost Analysis (Maliyet Analizi) › 4. Quick cost-reduction levers (design for manufacturing)

Fewer bends and fewer different bend radii/tools · allow a standard thickness and grade · avoid features that need new tools · nest-friendly shapes (common-line cutting) · loosen tolerances that do not matter · avoid secondary operations (tapping, deburr by hand) · combine parts when function allows · minimise painted area/ masking · standard fasteners.

docs.title: Sheet-Metal Cost Analysis (Maliyet Analizi)
docs.text:
Sheet-Metal Cost Analysis (Maliyet Analizi) › 5. Margin vs markup

`markup = (price − cost)/cost`, `margin = (price − cost)/price`. Always label which one the user means.

docs.title: Sheet-Metal Cost Analysis (Maliyet Analizi)
docs.text:
Sheet-Metal Cost Analysis (Maliyet Analizi) › 6. Sensitivity and uncertainty

Report ranges: material ± price change, yield ± 5 points, machine time ± 10–20 %. Show the **top 3 drivers**. If a rate is guessed, mark it `[ASSUMPTION]` and list it among the open items.

docs.title: Sheet-Metal Cost Analysis (Maliyet Analizi)
docs.text:
Sheet-Metal Cost Analysis (Maliyet Analizi) › 7. Output template

1. Inputs and assumptions table. 2. Cost breakdown table. 3. Unit price and lot price at quantity breaks. 4. Sensitivity (top drivers). 5. Open items (needed rates/prices). 6. Statement: illustrative if rates are not supplied.

docs.title: SolidWorks Macros and API (Makro ve API)
docs.text:
SolidWorks Macros and API (Makro ve API) › Overview

# SolidWorks Macros and API (Makro ve API)

docs.title: SolidWorks Macros and API (Makro ve API)
docs.section: 1. Why macros are risky for an AI to write
docs.text:
SolidWorks Macros and API (Makro ve API) › 1. Why macros are risky for an AI to write

The SolidWorks API is large and changes between releases (members are added as `...2`, `...3` versions, older ones are obsolete). A model that "remembers" an API call can invent a member or use the wrong argument list. The macro will either not compile, silently do nothing, or **modify the file wrongly**. The library therefore uses strict rules.

docs.title: SolidWorks Macros and API (Makro ve API)
docs.text:
SolidWorks Macros and API (Makro ve API) › 2. Rules for generated macros

1. Ask for: SolidWorks version, document type (Part/Assembly/Drawing), what is selected, desired result, whether the macro may modify the file.
2. Use only API members the AI can name with certainty; mark every other call `' VERIFY: check IModelDoc2 members in API Help for your version`.
3. **Read-only first.** Start with macros that read and report; add write operations (properties, save, export) only when requested.
4. Always check for `Nothing`: no active document, wrong document type, empty selection.
5. Never delete features/files in a first version; never overwrite the original; write output next to it with a new name.
6. Add `Option Explicit`, clear variable types, error handling, a message at the end that says what was done.
7. API names are English even in a Turkish interface; message texts to the user may be Turkish.
8. Tell the user to **test on a copy** and to save before running.
9. Do not claim the macro was run or tested unless the user supplied the result.
10. Avoid selecting by display names that change with language; prefer type-based traversal.

docs.title: SolidWorks Macros and API (Makro ve API)
docs.section: 3. Skeleton A — report the document and its mass (read-only, VBA)
docs.text:
SolidWorks Macros and API (Makro ve API) › 3. Skeleton A — report the document and its mass (read-only, VBA)

```vb
Option Explicit
Dim swApp As SldWorks.SldWorks

Sub main()
    Set swApp = Application.SldWorks
    Dim swModel As SldWorks.ModelDoc2
    Set swModel = swApp.ActiveDoc
    If swModel Is Nothing Then
        MsgBox "Açık belge yok."
        Exit Sub
    End If

    Dim swMass As SldWorks.MassProperty
    Set swMass = swModel.Extension.CreateMassProperty   ' VERIFY: newer versions may offer CreateMassProperty2
    If swMass Is Nothing Then
        MsgBox "Kütle özellikleri alınamadı."
        Exit Sub
    End If

    MsgBox swModel.GetTitle & vbCrLf & _
           "Kütle (kg): " & Format(swMass.Mass, "0.000") & vbCrLf & _
           "Hacim (m^3): " & Format(swMass.Volume, "0.000000")
End Sub
```
Notes: mass depends on the material assigned in the model and on the active configuration; the value is **calculated**, not weighed.

docs.title: SolidWorks Macros and API (Makro ve API)
docs.section: 4. Skeleton B — write a custom property (modifies the file)
docs.text:
SolidWorks Macros and API (Makro ve API) › 4. Skeleton B — write a custom property (modifies the file)

```vb
Option Explicit
Dim swApp As SldWorks.SldWorks

Sub main()
    Set swApp = Application.SldWorks
    Dim swModel As SldWorks.ModelDoc2
    Set swModel = swApp.ActiveDoc
    If swModel Is Nothing Then Exit Sub

    Dim swPropMgr As SldWorks.CustomPropertyManager
    Set swPropMgr = swModel.Extension.CustomPropertyManager("")   ' "" = file-level properties

    Dim rc As Long
    rc = swPropMgr.Add3("Revision", swCustomInfoType_e.swCustomInfoText, "A", _
                        swCustomPropertyAddOption_e.swCustomPropertyReplaceValue)
    ' VERIFY: interpret rc with the Add3 return enumeration in API Help
    MsgBox "Revision özelliği yazıldı. Dosyayı kaydetmeyi unutmayın."
End Sub
```
Notes: the property name is a string chosen by the user's template; property names created in a Turkish session keep their Turkish text. Configuration-specific properties use the configuration name instead of `""`.

docs.title: SolidWorks Macros and API (Makro ve API)
docs.text:
SolidWorks Macros and API (Makro ve API) › 5. Skeleton C — list configuration names

```vb
Dim names As Variant
names = swModel.GetConfigurationNames
Dim i As Long
For i = LBound(names) To UBound(names)
    Debug.Print names(i)
Next i
```

docs.title: SolidWorks Macros and API (Makro ve API)
docs.section: 6. Typical macro tasks (and the risk of each)
docs.text:
SolidWorks Macros and API (Makro ve API) › 6. Typical macro tasks (and the risk of each)

| Task | Risk | Safer approach |
|---|---|---|
| Fill title-block properties | Overwriting | Only-if-new option; log old values |
| Batch export DXF of flat patterns | Wrong flat/bend-line options, configuration | Export one part first; inspect the DXF; use the export-options API of the installed version (verify) |
| Rename/renumber files | Broken references | Prefer PDM or CAD rename tools; macro only logs |
| Update drawing revision tables | Version differences | Read first, write later |
| Apply a material or finish | Wrong density → wrong mass | Use library materials; verify result |
| Batch STEP export | Large assemblies slow | Test one |

docs.title: SolidWorks Macros and API (Makro ve API)
docs.text:
SolidWorks Macros and API (Makro ve API) › 7. Debugging checklist

Compile error · type-library references missing (SldWorks, swconst) · `Nothing` objects · wrong document type · array bounds · version difference · 64-bit vs 32-bit declarations (`PtrSafe`) · running macros from a network path.

docs.title: SolidWorks Macros and API (Makro ve API)
docs.text:
SolidWorks Macros and API (Makro ve API) › 8. Security

Run only macros from trusted sources; review code before running; keep macro security enabled; never run a macro that downloads or executes external code unless you wrote it.

docs.title: SolidWorks Macros and API (Makro ve API)
docs.section: 9. What the AI must say when unsure
docs.text:
SolidWorks Macros and API (Makro ve API) › 9. What the AI must say when unsure
